The archaeologist bases their claim on the fact that the hyena bone has nine evenly spaced, approximately parallel notches, but if the site primarily features examples of unevenly spaced parallel lines, that would suggest that the Neanderthals weren’t responsible for the notch marks on the bone. Also, if the hyena bones with even spacing were more common, it might suggest that the findings support the assertion of alternative hypotheses of stone-age cultures.
